Read a table's rows

Source: R/read.R
lake_read.Rd

lake_read() returns the rows of a snapshot as a data frame. It prunes the live files with filter first, so that only the files whose rows could match are read, then reads each one with qio, adds the partition columns from the log, keeps the rows filter is TRUE for, and binds the pieces. lake_walk() does the same one file at a time and calls FUN on each piece instead of binding them, for tables larger than memory.

Usage

lake_read(tbl, columns = NULL, filter = NULL, int64 = c("double", "integer64"))

lake_walk(
  tbl,
  FUN,
  columns = NULL,
  filter = NULL,
  int64 = c("double", "integer64")
)

Arguments

tbl

A snapshot, from lake_open().

columns

Columns to return, a character vector of column names, in that order. NULL, the default, returns every column qio can return.

filter

An expression over column names; see Details. NULL, the default, keeps every row.

int64

How 64-bit integers reach R, in data and partition columns: "double" (the default), exact up to 2^53 (qio returns NA with a warning past it, and a long partition value past 2^53 - 1 is an error of class zulake_error_int64), or "integer64" from the bit64 package.

FUN

A function, called with each piece: a data frame of one file's matching rows, in the same columns as lake_read() returns. Files without a matching row are skipped.

Value

lake_read() returns a data frame with one column per column asked for and one row per matching row, in the order of the files in lake_files() and of the rows in each file. lake_walk() returns NULL, invisibly.

Details

filter is an unevaluated R expression over column names, with values from the calling environment (a column's name always means the column). Its pruning subset is comparisons (==, !=, <, <=, >, >=), %in% and is.na() between a column and values, joined by !, & and |. That subset rules files out by their partition values and their statistics (minimum, maximum, null count and record count). Statistics only decide what is read: the rows returned are the rows filter is TRUE for whatever the statistics say, and a missing statistic only means a file is read.

A filter may also apply these row-wise functions to columns: +, -, *, /, %%, %/%, ^, abs(), round(), floor(), ceiling(), sqrt(), exp(), log(), nchar(), toupper(), tolower(), substr(), startsWith(), endsWith(), grepl(), is.nan(), is.finite(), xor(), as.character(), as.numeric() and as.integer(); and compare two columns, or use a logical column alone. R evaluates those on the rows after reading (they never prune), with base R's functions whatever the caller defines, and each must give one TRUE, FALSE or NA per row. Any other call with a column inside it, such as max(x), mean(x), rank(x), cumsum(x), duplicated(x), x[1], %in% with a column on its right, or a function of your own, is an error of class zulake_error_filter: a filter is decided row by row, so the rows it keeps do not depend on how the table's rows are split into files, and lake_read() equals the pieces of lake_walk() bound together. A part of the filter that names no column is a value, evaluated once where lake_read() is called, and may be any R expression.

Inside the pruning subset, comparisons are exact: a long, integer, short, byte or decimal column is compared with the value as decimal numbers, digit by digit, and a string column in UTF-8 byte order whatever the session's collation, as the table's statistics are. A value given as text, such as "12.30", is read as that decimal number; a double that has no exact decimal form of 15 digits (1/3, 0.1 + 0.2) is an error asking for the value as text. A date or timestamp column takes a Date or POSIXct, or text such as "2024-01-31" or "2024-01-31 12:00:00" (UTC unless it gives an offset).

Columns are typed as qio returns them (see qio::read_parquet()), and partition columns as lake_files() types them, except that a decimal of precision 15 or less, data or partition, is a double, which holds it exactly. Columns qio cannot return are not lost silently: nested columns (struct, array, map) and decimals of precision above 15, until qio reads them. With columns = NULL they are left out, each named in a warning of class zulake_warning_column_skipped (fields column and reason); named in columns or used in filter, such a column is an error of class zulake_error_column_unreadable with the same fields.

Data files are read in place on local disk; other stores download each file once per session, to the session's temporary directory.

Rows a deletion vector marks as deleted are never returned (see lake_deletion_vectors()); reading their vectors needs the zuroar package, and without it a read of a table with deletion vectors in the files it reads is an error of class zulake_error_missing_package. Every such vector is read and checked before any data file, so a corrupt one (zulake_error_corrupt_log) returns no rows. A table that maps column names (column mapping in name mode) is read by each column's physical name in the files and returned with its logical names; a timestamp_ntz column is a POSIXct in UTC.

See also

lake_files() to see which files a filter keeps, lake_count() for the number of rows from the log alone.

Examples

# A partitioned table of two files: the data written with qio, the log by
# hand.
path <- tempfile("table")
dir.create(file.path(path, "_delta_log"), recursive = TRUE)
add <- function(year, ids) {
  file <- sprintf("year=%d/part-0.parquet", year)
  dir.create(file.path(path, dirname(file)))
  qio::write_parquet(data.frame(id = ids), file.path(path, file))
  sprintf(
    paste0(
      '{"add":{"path":"%s","partitionValues":{"year":"%d"},"size":%.0f,',
      '"modificationTime":0,"dataChange":true,"stats":"{\\"numRecords\\":%d,',
      '\\"minValues\\":{\\"id\\":%g},\\"maxValues\\":{\\"id\\":%g},',
      '\\"nullCount\\":{\\"id\\":0}}"}}'
    ),
    file, year, file.size(file.path(path, file)), length(ids), min(ids), max(ids)
  )
}
writeLines(c(
  '{"protocol":{"minReaderVersion":1,"minWriterVersion":2}}',
  paste0(
    '{"metaData":{"id":"example","format":{"provider":"parquet","options":{}},',
    '"schemaString":"{\\"type\\":\\"struct\\",\\"fields\\":[',
    '{\\"name\\":\\"id\\",\\"type\\":\\"double\\",\\"nullable\\":true,\\"metadata\\":{}},',
    '{\\"name\\":\\"year\\",\\"type\\":\\"integer\\",\\"nullable\\":true,\\"metadata\\":{}}]}",',
    '"partitionColumns":["year"],"configuration":{}}}'
  ),
  add(2025, c(1, 2, 3)),
  add(2026, c(4, 5))
), file.path(path, "_delta_log", "00000000000000000000.json"))

tbl <- lake_open(path)
lake_read(tbl)
#>   id year
#> 1  1 2025
#> 2  2 2025
#> 3  3 2025
#> 4  4 2026
#> 5  5 2026
lake_read(tbl, filter = id >= 3 & year == 2026)
#>   id year
#> 1  4 2026
#> 2  5 2026
# The statistics alone rule out the 2025 file for this filter:
lake_files(tbl, filter = id > 3)$path
#> [1] "year=2026/part-0.parquet"
lake_walk(tbl, function(piece) print(nrow(piece)))
#> [1] 3
#> [1] 2

unlink(path, recursive = TRUE)
